corpus.sampling_rule: none — complete enumeration of the space, then one representative per orbit
corpus.citation: Rapoport & Guyer (1966); Robinson & Goforth (2005) — external provenance of the space
corpus.note: complete enumeration; the §5 kill 'corpus selected using desired placements' cannot fire on a complete space

native_encoder.description: the eight ordinal payoff ranks, the space's own standard representation

target.ground_truth: computed from payoff ranks by definition; no model, no interpretation

splits.scheme: deterministic stratified 6-fold over the complete space
splits.development: folds 1-4 (feature selection for ONE_AXIS and LEARNED_NO_PLACEMENT touched only these)
splits.note: reported scores are the mean across all 6 rotations; per-fold min and max are in m4_run_result.json

resource_parity.learner: identical depth-3, 8-leaf decision tree for every representation

kill: KILLED on this corpus and comparator class. The four-axis encoding scored macro_f1 0.2817 on the primary target against a majority baseline of 0.2815 — no signal — and lost to all four required comparators. Three §5 kills fired: (1) a generic representation matched or beat it at lower code length (ONE_AXIS 0.5778 at 135 bits vs 0.2817 at 542; on is_dilemma ONE_AXIS matched it exactly at 89 bits vs 536); (2) the ADDED_AXIS comparator produced a large held-out gain (+0.61 macro_f1 on the primary target from one added axis); (3) it fell below the frozen 0.8 floor on every target. On nash_pareto — the ego/collective question, its own home turf — it scored 0.4464, BELOW the 0.4545 majority baseline. The missing-placement penalty is not the cause: M4_TWO_LIVE_AXES, carrying no missing-placement cost, scored identically on all four targets.
survivor: Per §5 the chart survives as a visualization, interpretive vocabulary and hypothesis generator; it does not survive as a measured optimal code. SCOPE OF THIS KILL, stated narrowly: one corpus (one-shot strictly ordinal 2x2 games, complete, n=78), four targets, one learner, one comparator class. Axes 3 and 4 (physical/represented power, short/long horizon) have NO REFERENT in a one-shot ordinal game and were recorded as costed missing placements rather than assigned by an undisclosed rule. This result therefore does not test the four-axis encoding on corpora where those axes denote — repeated games, policies, corpora with information structure or a horizon. Such a corpus is the obvious next run and the harness accepts one unchanged.
